lines: I have handled sharp nights before. This one nearly handled me back.
Still here, still got all my fingers, still not eager to repeat it.
I came back with a shaking hand and an empty stomach. Better than not coming back.
There was too much noise and not enough door between me and it. I found the door.
I have had hard mornings, but that night was something else entirely.
My apron has seen worse stains. My nerves have not.
I made it home, and I am counting that before I count anything else.
The cleaver stayed in my grip. So did my sense, barely.
I used the cleaver for something it was never meant to do and hated every moment.
The smell of blood followed me home, though none of it came from the block.
I wrapped my own arm with the cloth meant for tomorrow's work.
A food barrel stopped the first blow and split down the middle.
The animals panicked before I understood where the attack had started.
I kept thinking about the smokehouse door I had left open.
My grip failed after the danger passed, not during it.
We shared the last strip of jerky while waiting for a safe road home.
I know how deep a cut is by sight. Mine was deep enough to frighten me.
Someone watched my back while I pulled a wounded neighbor clear.
The fight ended, but every hanging hook looked dangerous for days.
I came home hungry and could not make myself eat.
